'''Saeki clan''' (佐伯氏) refers to a group of families bearing the name "Saeki" as their {{ill|Uji (clan)|en|Uji (clan)|qid=Q2575910|lt=Uji}} (clan name).

__TOC__{{-}}

== Overview ==
The Saeki clan traces its origins to {{ill|Ama-no-Oshihi|ja|天押日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenootsuhiko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシヒ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10939616|2=ja|3=アメノオシヒ|4=zh|5=天忍日命}} (Ame no Oshi-hi no Mikoto), who guided {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|彦火瓊々杵尊|lt=Ninigi}} during the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|qid=Q1084733|lt=Descent of the heavenly grandson}}. The clan split from the {{ill|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|en|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|qid=Q17227938|lt=Ōtomo clan}} under the leadership of {{ill|Ōtomo Muroya|ja|大伴室屋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtomo no Muroya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11432336}}, becoming a {{ill|Shinbetsu|ja|神別}} (descendant of deities) lineage of {{ill|Amatsukami and Kunitsukami|ja|天津神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11442793}} origin. The clan name "Saeki" is believed to derive from their role in guarding the imperial court, as they were seen as those who "block (遮 sahe) external threats." This evolved into "Saeki" (さえき) in modern phonetics, and in some cases as "Saiki" (さゐき).

The Saeki clan served as {{ill|Tomonomiyatsuko|ja|伴造}}, leading the {{ill|Saeki people|en|Saeki people|qid=Q7398288|lt=Saeki-be}}, who were tasked with guarding the {{ill|Royal court|en|Royal court|qid=Q1134237|lt=Imperial Court of Japan}}. The gates they protected were named "Saeki Gates," though during the Heian period, under {{ill|Tenpyō culture|ja|唐風文化|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tang culture|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天平文化|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5525117}} influences, the name was changed to "Mokabe Gate" (藻壁門). Initially granted the {{ill|Kabane|ja|姓}} of "Muraji" (連), the Saeki clan, alongside the Ōtomo clan and others, was elevated to the Rank of "Sukune" (宿禰) during the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign (685 CE).

Prominent figures in the Saeki clan included {{ill|Saeki no Komaro|ja|佐伯子麻呂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Komaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382809}}, who assisted in the assassination of Soga no Iruka, and {{ill|Saeki no Imaemishi|ja|佐伯今毛人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Imaemaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382787}}, a statesman who served as a {{ill|Sangi (Japan)|en|Sangi (Japan)|qid=Q1133663|lt=Sangi}} and {{ill|Dazai no Sochi|ja|太宰帥}}. Military leaders such as {{ill|Saeki no Nifute|ja|佐伯丹経手|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Tsurugite|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q45828498}}, who served under Soga no Umako, and {{ill|Saeki no Iwayu|ja|佐伯石湯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Ishiyu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382879}}, a general during campaigns against the Emishi, were also notable. However, by the end of the Heian period, the clan gradually declined from mid-level aristocracy to {{ill|Jigeke|ja|地下家|2=ja|3=地下家|lt=Jigeke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikage|13=User:Immanuelle/Jigeke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11424052}} (bureaucrats of lower Rank).

The Saeki name was carried on by families like the Ono family, who produced the herbalist {{ill|Ono Ranzan|en|Ono Ranzan|qid=Q11464264|lt=Ono Ranzan}}, and artists such as {{ill|Kishi Ganku|en|Kishi Ganku|qid=Q555061|lt=Kishi Ganku}} of the Kishi school.

== Related Lineages ==
=== Saeki no Miyatsuko (佐伯造)
The Saeki no Miyatsuko lineage is documented in the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}, appearing under the {{ill|Ukyo|en|Ukyo|qid=Q2474484|lt=Right Capital}} Shinbetsu. They were originally known as "Saeki-be" and managed the Saeki-be labor group.

=== Saeki no Obito (佐伯首)
The Saeki no Obito line appears in the Shinbetsu of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}} as recorded in the Shinsen Shōjiroku.

== Saeki-be ==
The Saeki-be, managed by the central Saeki clan, was a labor group organized as part of the {{ill|Shinabe clans|en|Shinabe clans|qid=Q11418456|lt=Shinbetsu}} system. Local Saeki-be groups were supervised by the {{ill|Nao Saeki|ja|佐伯直|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki no Ason|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382874}} lineage.

'''Saeki Clan''' (佐伯氏) is a {{ill|Uji (clan)|en|Uji (clan)|qid=Q2575910|lt=Uji}} whose name is "Saeki".

__TOC__{{-}}

== Overview ==
During the time of {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|qid=Q1084733|lt=Descent of the Heavenly Grandson}}, the ancestor, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1056017|lt=Hikohirakininomikoto}}, who was led by {{ill|Ama-no-Oshihi|de|Amenooshihi|ja|アメノオシヒ|lt=Heavenly Push Day Deity|lt_ja=天押日命|lt_de=Amenooshihi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenooshihi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10939616|2=ja|3=アメノオシヒ|4=zh|5=天忍日命}}, (Amenooshihi no Mikoto), is said to be the progenitor, and it is a {{ill|Shinbetsu|de|Divine Separation|ja|神別}} clan that split from the Otomo clan during the time of {{ill|Ōtomo Muroya|de|Otomo no Sukune|ja|大伴室屋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otomo no Sukune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11432336}} {{sfn|日本大百科全書}}<ref>‘{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=New Compilation of Surnames}}’ {{ill|Sakyo|en|Sakyo|qid=Q11479660|lt=Sakyo}}, in the Divine Separation section.</ref>. After serving the royal authority and undertaking duties such as palace security, there is a theory that they came to be called "Saeki", a term meaning "those who block" (遮ぎる者), referring to repelling external enemy attacks ({{ill|Historical kana orthography|en|Historical kana orthography|qid=Q1142552|lt=Historical Kana Usage}} spells it "saheki", while {{ill|Modern kana usage|en|Modern kana usage|qid=Q2572881|lt=Modern Kana Usage}} spells it "saeki"). There is also a dialectal pronunciation "saiki" (also "sawiki").

As the central {{ill|Tomonomiyatsuko|de|Banzō|ja|伴造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Banzō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11381545}}, they led the {{ill|Saeki people|en|Saeki people|qid=Q7398288|lt=Saeki Faction}}, serving the {{ill|Imperial Court of Japan|de|Kaiserhof|ja|朝廷 (日本)|lt=Imperial Court|lt_ja=朝廷|lt_de=Kaiserhof|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Court|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30253177}} as palace gate guards and as a military force. Incidentally, the palace gate in charge of security was named {{ill|Sōhekimon|de|Saeki-Tor|ja|佐伯門|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki Gate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藻壁門|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17995614}} after the clan name, but at the {{ill|Heian Palace|en|Heian Palace|qid=Q304501|lt=Heian Palace}}, under the influence of {{ill|Tenpyō culture|de|Tang-Kultur|ja|唐風文化|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tang-style Culture|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天平文化|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5525117}}, it was renamed to {{ill|Sōhekimon|de|Mooswandtor|ja|藻壁門|lt=Moss Wall Gate (Sōheki Gate)|lt_ja=藻壁（そうへき）門|lt_de=Mooswandtor|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moss Wall Gate|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17995614}}<ref>‘{{ill|Nihon Kiryaku|en|Nihon Kiryaku|qid=Q1053542|lt=Nihon Kiriyaku}}’ {{ill|Kōnin (era)|en|Kōnin (era)|qid=Q1373070|lt=Kōnin}} 9th year ({{ill|818|en|818|qid=Q25083|lt=818 AD}}) April 27 clause.</ref>. The {{ill|Kabane|en|Kabane|qid=Q1664099|lt=Surname}} was originally {{ill|Muraji|en|Muraji|qid=Q2735611|lt=Ren}}, but in the 13th year of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|qid=Q335181|lt=Emperor Tenmu}} ({{ill|685|en|685|qid=Q33480|lt=685 AD}}), together with members of the same group such as the {{ill|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|en|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|qid=Q17227938|lt=Otomo Clan}}, they were granted the surname {{ill|Sukune|en|Sukune|qid=Q11455653|lt=Sukunabe}}. In the {{ill|Shudenryō|de|Hauptpalastamt|ja|主殿寮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Main Palace Office|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11368767}}, the name of the Saeki faction remains as one of the noble divisions.

Notable figures include {{ill|Saeki no Komaro|de|Saeki Komaro|ja|佐伯子麻呂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki Komaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382809}}, who, following {{ill|Emperor Tenji|de|Prinz Nakano-Ōe|ja|中大兄皇子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Nakano-Ōe|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天智天皇|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q314802}}, assassinated {{ill|Soga no Iruka|en|Soga no Iruka|qid=Q736621|lt=Soga no Iruka}}, and {{ill|Saeki no Imaemishi|de|Saeki Imao Hito|ja|佐伯今毛人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki Imao Hito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382787}}, who was active in government from the Nara to the Heian period and held positions such as {{ill|Sangi (Japan)|en|Sangi (Japan)|qid=Q1133663|lt=Sangi}} and {{ill|Dazai no Sochi|de|Dazai no Mikoto|ja|太宰帥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dazai no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大宰帥|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11434484}}. The clan also produced many warriors, including {{ill|Saeki no Nifute|de|Saeki Tankeide|ja|佐伯丹経手|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki Tankeide|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q45828498}} (the father of Komaro), who, following {{ill|Soga no Umako|en|Soga no Umako|qid=Q1191233|lt=Soga no Umako}}, executed {{ill|Prince Anahobe|de|Prinz Anahobe|ja|穴穂部皇子}}; {{ill|Saeki no Iwayu|de|Saeki Ishiyu|ja|佐伯石湯|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki Ishiyu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382879}}, the Ezo General after the conquest of Echigo; and {{ill|Saeki no Kazuragi|de|Saeki Katsuragi|ja|佐伯葛城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki Katsuragi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382895}} (the grandson of Ishiyu), the Deputy General of the Eastern Expedition.

Apart from Imao Hito, no one ascended to the position of {{ill|Giseikan|de|Giseikan|ja|議政官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Giseikan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11632467}} {{sfn|日本大百科全書}}, and the clan eventually declined from being mid-level nobles to lower-Ranked officials ({{ill|Jigeke|de|Underground Officials|ja|地下家|2=ja|3=地下家|lt=Jigeke|lt=Underground Officials|lt_ja=地下官人|lt_de=Underground Officials|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Underground Officials|13=User:Immanuelle/Jigeke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11424052}}). Until around the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|Sengoku period|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku Period}}, together with the {{ill|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|en|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|qid=Q17227938|lt=Otomo Clan}}, {{ill|Wake clan|de|Wake Clan|ja|和気氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wake Clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11417729}}, and the {{ill|Kudara no Konikishi clan|en|Kudara no Konikishi clan|qid=Q710197|lt=Baekje Royal Family}}, the clan was considered one that received {{ill|Imperial, royal and noble ranks|en|Imperial, royal and noble ranks|qid=Q355567|lt=Noble Titles}} upon the accession of an emperor<ref>{{ill|Isao Tajima|de|Tajima no Kimoto|ja|田島公|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tajima no Kimoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q45819717}} "The Establishment of Noble Titles – Rituals, Service, and Conferment" in {{sfn|史林}} 71-1, {{ill|1988|en|1988|qid=Q2426|lt=1988 AD}}, p. 61</ref>.

Among the lower-Ranked officials bearing the Saeki name, there is the {{ill|Ono Family|de|Ono-Familie|ja|小野家 (佐伯姓)|lt=Ono Family}}, which produced the materia medica scholar {{ill|Ono Ranzan|en|Ono Ranzan|qid=Q11464264|lt=Ono Ransan}}, and the painter {{ill|Kishi Ganku|en|Kishi Ganku|qid=Q555061|lt=Kishi Koma}}, who founded the {{ill|Kishi school|de|Kishi-Schule|ja|岸派|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kishi School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11475951}} and served the {{ill|Arisugawa-no-miya|en|Arisugawa-no-miya|qid=Q2861427|lt=Arisugawa-no-miya}} family, bearing the Saeki name.

== Related Clans ==
=== Saeki Tsukuri ===
'''Saeki Tsukuri''' (-Miyatsuko) appears in the ‘{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=New Compilation of Surnames}}’ under the {{ill|Ukyo|en|Ukyo|qid=Q2474484|lt=Right Capital}} Divine Separation section, and his former name was "Saeki Faction". According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, he was a retainer of {{ill|Ichinobe no Oshiwa|en|Ichinobe no Oshiwa|qid=Q2297842|lt=Ichinobe Oshi}} and a descendant of {{ill|Saekibe no Uruwa|de|Saeki Fraktion Naka-chiko|ja|佐伯部仲子|lt=Naka-chiko|lt_ja=なかちこ|lt_de=Naka-chiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki Faction Naka-chiko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 佐伯部売輪|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q85876437}}<ref>In the Pre-accession Annals of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|en|Emperor Yūryaku|qid=Q357235|lt=Emperor Yūryaku}}, in the 3rd year, October 1 clause of {{ill|Emperor Ankō|en|Emperor Ankō|qid=Q361010|lt=Emperor Ankan}}, he is referred to as "Saeki Faction Uruba" (–uruba), also known as "Naka-teko" (なかちこ).</ref> and, in the 5th year, February 5 clause of {{ill|Emperor Ninken|en|Emperor Ninken|qid=Q357266|lt=Emperor Ninken}}, he was appointed to oversee the Saeki factions from various provinces.

=== Saeki Obito ===
'''Saeki Obito''' (-Obito) appears in the ‘{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=New Compilation of Surnames}}’ in {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}} under the {{ill|Shinbetsu|de|Divine Separation|ja|神別}} category.

== Saeki Faction ==
The Saeki Clan oversaw the central {{ill|Saeki people|en|Saeki people|qid=Q7398288|lt=Saeki Faction}} within the {{ill|Shinabe clans|en|Shinabe clans|qid=Q11418456|lt=Official Division}},<ref>{{Cite kotobank|Saeki Clan|encyclopedia=Sekai Dai Hyakka Jiten 2nd edition|accessdate=2021-12-19}}</ref> while the regional Saeki Faction was overseen by {{ill|Nao Saeki|de|Saeki Nao|ja|佐伯直|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saeki Nao|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11382874}} {{sfn|日本大百科全書}}.
